name: Agoragentic Integrations

hlido_opinion.headline: A 97-surface integration catalogue for a governed agent router, notable mostly for refusing to let its own status labels be misread as live availability.
hlido_opinion.body: Agoragentic positions itself as a governed routing, commerce and receipt layer: keep your model loop and local tools in whatever framework you already use, send external work through `execute()`, and carry invocation, policy, cost and settlement evidence back as a receipt. This catalogue is the integration surface — 97 manifest-backed entries, 34 first-class site guides, 63 repo adapters and references, with a stated catalog source date of 2026-07-23 and newly indexed entries for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Cline. The distribution shape is sensible (npm, PyPI, an MCP relay, and a local harness for no-spend policy and readiness runs), and the three-step buyer flow — match, execute, prove — is coherent. The standout is a disclaimer most catalogues would omit: "Statuses describe the public integration artifact, not live paid-route availability", and experimental entries stay guides or references unless their repository evidence says otherwise. That is precise, self-limiting language, and it is the main reason to take the counts seriously. Against that: the counts are self-reported and we verified none of them; a catalogue of adapters is not evidence that routing, commerce or settlement work in production; there are no named customers or transaction volumes; and the governance and policy claims — the actual product — sit behind this surface where we could not see them. Dating the catalogue is good practice and also a liability, since a stale date is now visible to everyone.

tier_rationale: FADING (68) — the surface is careful and well-organised, and the explicit warning that statuses describe artifacts rather than live paid-route availability is unusually honest. But this is a catalogue of integration artifacts, not evidence of a working routing, commerce and settlement layer: all counts are self-reported and unverified, there are no named customers or volumes, and the governed-router product itself sits behind the page we captured.
what_it_does_well: Explicitly warns that statuses describe the public integration artifact, not live paid-route availability
Experimental entries stay guides or references unless repository evidence supports more
Catalogue carries a visible source date (2026-07-23) so readers can judge freshness
Coherent three-step buyer flow — match (preview), execute (route), prove (receipt)
Sensible distribution: npm and PyPI SDKs, an MCP relay, and a local harness for no-spend policy and readiness runs
Does not require moving your model loop, memory runtime or local tools into a hosted control plane
what_it_fails_at: All headline counts (97 surfaces, 34 guides, 63 adapters) are self-reported and unverified by Hlido
An integration catalogue is not evidence that routing, commerce or settlement work in production
No named customers, transaction volumes, or third-party validation
The governed router — the actual product — is not visible on this surface, so it could not be assessed
A dated catalogue becomes visibly stale if it is not maintained; nothing states the refresh cadence
No pricing on the captured surface despite commerce being central to the pitch
best_for: Teams already running an agent framework who want external work routed through one governed rail
Buyers who need invocation, policy, cost and settlement evidence carried back as receipts
Developers checking whether their specific runtime already has an adapter
not_recommended_for: Anyone treating the catalogue's status labels as proof a paid route is live — the vendor says it is not
Procurement needing verified transaction volumes or reference customers
Teams wanting a complete agent platform rather than a routing and settlement layer

evidence_urls.claim: 97 manifest-backed surfaces, 34 first-class site guides, 63 repo adapters and references

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Node and Python SDKs plus an MCP relay (`npx agoragentic-mcp`) and a POST /api/execute rail; the whole design assumes an agent framework calls it rather than a human using a dashboard.
